title: Operator upgrade rewrote tenant runtime when ExternalSecret fetch failed — add preflight checksum and safe rollback
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: A recent operator upgrade path caused tenant runtime config to be partially overwritten when the ExternalSecret controller returned transient errors (502/503). In multiple customer escalations the upgrade proceeded and a helm post-upgrade hook applied an empty Secret manifest, replacing the live secret for a subset of tenants and triggering downstream KV cache invalidation and service disruptions. This ticket scopes an investigation fix and a hotfix release that prevents destructive writes during upgrade when ExternalSecret resolution is degraded, plus a preflight checksum validation to block unsafe upgrades.
reproduction_steps:
1) Install on-prem operator at v3.1.8 with ExternalSecret CRD enabled for tenants A/B/C.
2) Configure an ExternalSecret pointing at an external secret manager that will intermittently return 502 for ~5s windows.
3) Trigger operator upgrade to v3.2.0 that includes the helm post-upgrade hook that reconciles secrets.
4) Observe that when the ExternalSecret fetch fails, the reconciler creates an empty Secret object (nil data) and helm considers hook successful, overwriting the tenant secret.
5) Result: tenant runtime sees missing credentials, nodeagent restarts, KV cache invalidates and traffic errors spike.
Repro rate observed in stage: ~20% when ExternalSecret experiences transient 502s during upgrade window.
investigation_summary:
Root cause: operator upgrade path executes a reconcile flow that constructs Secret manifests from ExternalSecret fetch results. The code path treated fetch error as 'no data' rather than a transient failure, so it emitted an empty Secret which helm/helm-hooks applied. Secondary cause: no preflight validation existed to compare current live secret checksum against expected post-upgrade manifest; operator assumed idempotence. Telemetry: we correlated customer incident timelines with ExternalSecret controller logs showing 502 spikes. Also found helm hook timeout set to 30s which masked fetch retries.
Related findings: ExternalSecret controller clients sometimes backoff which increased chance of nil-result being interpreted as success. There was no upgrade-blocking annotation for unresolved secret fetches.
proposed_fix: 1) Hotfix operator-3.2.1: change reconcile to be idempotent and defensive — do not write a Secret when ExternalSecret resolution returns an error; instead annotate the ExternalSecret with status 'upgrade-blocker' and emit a metric and event. 2) Introduce preflight checksum pass: before applying helm post-upgrade hooks, compute a stable SHA256 digest of the existing Secret manifest (sorted keys, deterministic serialization) and compare to the desired manifest; if the desired manifest cannot be produced because of ExternalSecret resolution failure, fail the preflight and mark tenant as 'upgrade-pending'. 3) Add a staged canary rollout policy: block upgrades by default for tenants with unresolved secrets; allow opt-in 'force-override' for internal debugging only. 4) Increase helm hook timeout for secret resolution to 120s and add retry logic in the ExternalSecret fetch path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Operator release operator-3.2.1 prevents empty-secret overwrites during upgrade on degraded ExternalSecret.
- Preflight checksum step implemented and returns non-zero exit code when ExternalSecret cannot be resolved for a tenant.
- Canary rollout executes on 1% tenant sample without causing overwrite incidents.
- Automated unit+integration tests covering: ExternalSecret error path, checksum computation, annotation set, and helm hook dry-run behavior.
- Confluence runbook updated with postmortem and remediation steps.
- Metrics/alerts: 'externalsecret.resolve.failures' and 'upgrade.blocked.tenants' created and wired to SRE pager for P0 customers.
implementation_plan:
Phase A (hotfix, 2 days): apply defensive change to reconciler to never write an empty Secret on fetch error; add annotation and metric. Release operator-3.2.1 to dedicated and private clusters with manual canary.
Phase B (preflight, 3 days): implement preflight checksum/dry-run in operator upgrade controller; hook into upgrade orchestration to block if checksums cannot be computed. Add helm dry-run step in upgrade pipeline.
Phase C (rollout/observability, 2 days): add alerts, dashboards, telemetry, and runbook. Restore normal upgrade runbook with automatic retry windows and human override mechanisms.
Rollback strategy: operator-3.2.1 is non-destructive; if issues arise, rollback to v3.1.8 using staged rollback with tenant-level fencing and replay of secrets from backup if any overwrite occurred.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: checksum computation, deterministic serialization.
- Integration tests: simulate ExternalSecret controller 502s and assert operator does not create empty Secret.
- E2E: deploy to internal staging tenants and run upgrade with fault-injection (chaos) for ExternalSecret.
- Canary: release to test tenants (1%) then to low-risk production tenants, monitor metrics for 48h before full rollout.
rollback_plan:
- If a destructive overwrite is observed post-release: 1) Pause rollout across remaining tenants. 2) For affected tenants, run secret-restore script to reapply last-good secret from backup (S3 snapshot of Secret manifests taken by operator backup job). 3) Roll back operator to v3.1.8 for tenant-group if manual restore not possible. 4) Execute post-incident migration to reconcile differences and root cause.
- All steps codified in runbook link below.
